passage:
A school project asked students to make a language map of their neighborhood. They recorded signs in different languages on stores, temples, clinics, and restaurants.
They found more languages than expected. Some were used for business, some for religion, and some for communities that had moved there from other places.
The map showed the neighborhood as a living record of migration and contact.
Students learned that language is not only spoken at home or taught in school. It appears on walls, menus, doors, and street signs.
A city can speak many languages at once. People only need to slow down and read it.
